initial_presentation: A 73-year-old male patient presented with a two-month history of sudden onset numbness and gradual weakness in the lower extremities, leading to walking difficulties. Ten days prior to admission, the symptoms progressed to paraparesis. The patient was transferred from a primary healthcare facility and has a past medical history of controlled hypertension and type II diabetes mellitus. The patient also has a history of chronic pelvic pain syndrome. There was no evidence of prostate cancer or any other primary systemic tumor. Additionally, there was no evidence of any spinal or intracranial lesion. Cerebrospinal fluid examination was negative for malignant cells.
An 11-year-old girl visited the outpatient department in August 2016 due to abdominal pain.

Case 1 involves a 19-year-old woman. She was born at 37 weeks gestation with a birth weight of 2890 g, length of 47 cm, and a head circumference of 32 cm. Both pre- and neonatal periods were normal. At 5 months of age, she experienced her first seizure, which was prolonged and febrile. Subsequently, she developed afebrile focal seizures and intractable generalized seizures, including myotonic, tonic, and tonic-clonic types. She has had multiple episodes of convulsive status epilepticus. Her early development was initially typical; she developed normal hand function, including a pincer grip, and used up to 15 words. She began walking independently at 17 months. However, from around 15 months, her developmental progress slowed, and she gradually lost previously acquired skills. She ceased using her hands, lost her spoken words, and her gait became broad-based and ataxic. She developed midline rubbing hand movements, bruxism, breath-holding spells, and occasional hyperventilation. Her sleep was disrupted with nighttime screaming and occasional laughing spells. Between one and two years of age, she exhibited autistic traits and experienced a deceleration in head growth from the 50th to the 10th percentile. At 19 years old, clinical examination showed intense eye contact, ongoing stereotypic hand movements with hand dyspraxia, a broad-based gait with notable ataxia, breath-holding, and teeth grinding. She was 141 cm tall with normal weight for her height. Her musculature was generally hypotonic, and she had a slight scoliosis. Despite intensive anti-epileptic treatment, she continued to have daily seizures (focal, tonic, and tonic-clonic).

A 26-year-old male reported experiencing painful urination and blood in the urine for approximately one month. During a digital rectal examination, a large, hard mass with an uneven surface was detected. The serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level was measured at 0.44 ng/mL, which is within the normal range. Additional tumor markers were also found to be within normal limits.

A 2-month-old full-term female infant was admitted with a one-month history of poor feeding and weight loss. The patient exhibited increased irritability, frequent vomiting, and a weight loss of 0.5 kg over the past month. Prior to admission, she was given oral probiotics (Bifidobacterium bifidum 0.5 g/kg/day for 7 days). Her birth and family history were unremarkable. Upon admission, her weight was 4 kg (−3 SD), and she was in poor mental and nutritional condition. Physical examination revealed a palpable mass measuring 3 cm × 4 cm in the upper left abdomen.

A 16-year-old female presented with epilepsy, developmental delay, and cerebellar atrophy. Muscle weakness was observed at 2 years old. At 1 year of age, she experienced clinical seizures characterized by twitching movements, staring episodes, cluster seizures, and spasms. By 18 months, there was only a partial response to anti-convulsive therapy. Global developmental delay was noted by 2 years old, with no speech development and a need for assistance with daily activities. She was vigorous as a newborn, passed her newborn disease screening, and began walking around 18 months. The patient is the second child in a non-consanguineous family; her mother was 33 years old at the time of birth. She was born at full term with normal birth parameters following a normal pregnancy with no known teratogenic exposure. There is no personal or family history of seizures. Clinical examination revealed deep-set eyes with nystagmus and a small nose with a nasal bridge.

A 12-year-old female presented with a primary concern of yellowish discoloration of her teeth, which she noted had been present since childhood. She also reported that her deciduous teeth exhibited similar discoloration. Clinical examination revealed mandibular prognathism, anterior open bite, generalized plaque and calculus deposits, yellowish discoloration of the teeth, and chipping of the incisal and cuspal enamel structures.

A 44-year-old woman arrived at the emergency department with a four-day history of cough and fever. The cough was dry, and the fever reached a peak of 38.1℃, which was alleviated with oral paracetamol. She did not experience chest pain or difficulty breathing. The patient had no prior health issues and was a non-smoker. Family and social history were unremarkable. Physical examination showed normal oxygen saturation and vital signs, including pulse and respiratory rates. Her body mass index was 28 kg/m2 (height 159 cm, weight 71 kg). Scattered crepitations were heard in both lung fields.
A 27-year-old male with no significant medical history presented with a painful furuncle in the right axillary region and moderate to high-grade fever.

A 7-year-old female exhibited breast development over a four-month period, accompanied by vaginal discharge and a noticeable increase in height. Her medical and family histories were unremarkable. She measured 130 cm in height (+2.24 standard deviation) and weighed 28.9 kg (+1.62 standard deviation). Physical examination showed breast development at Tanner stage 3, with no pubic or axillary hair present.
